step1_analysis.description: A single-balanced passive mixer utilizing NMOS switches to downconvert an RF signal to baseband/IF. The parallel NMOS transistors (e.g., XM1_N and XM1_P) are used in conjunction with a bias-shifting network to track LO DC offsets, which significantly improves the second-order intermodulation (IIP2) performance.

paper_reference.title: A CMOS Passive Mixer With Low Flicker Noise for Low-Power Direct-Conversion Receiver

Conversion Gain.description: The ratio of the downconverted IF output voltage amplitude to the RF input voltage amplitude.

sky130_expected.calculation: A bare passive mixer switch network has a theoretical minimum voltage conversion loss of 2/pi (approx -3.9 dB). The 3 dB gain reported in the paper likely includes an integrated IF transimpedance amplifier or resonant RF matching. For the isolated switch netlist in SKY130, we expect a conversion loss.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Theoretical 2/pi loss combined with finite switch on-resistance (Ron) voltage division against the load.

IIP3.description: Third-order input intercept point, indicating the linearity of the mixer against third-order intermodulation products.

sky130_expected.calculation: Passive mixers are highly linear because they operate the transistors in the deep triode region. IIP3 depends heavily on the LO gate overdrive voltage (Vgs - Vth). With LO DC at 0.75V and amplitude 0.6V, peak Vgs is 1.35V, providing strong overdrive.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Comparable to the 0.18um process, SKY130 1.8V devices driven with large LO swings will yield similar high linearity.

IIP2.description: Second-order input intercept point, critical for direct-conversion receivers to reject AM demodulation of interferers.

sky130_expected.calculation: The paper achieves 39 dBm using a unique bias-shifting network to track LO DC offsets. Assuming the external bias network is perfectly tuned in the testbench, similar performance can be achieved.
sky130_expected.reasoning: IIP2 in single-balanced passive mixers is highly dependent on device matching and LO duty cycle/offset compensation.

Flicker Noise Corner.description: The frequency at which the 1/f noise power equals the thermal noise floor.

sky130_expected.calculation: Passive mixers carry zero DC current, which inherently suppresses 1/f noise. The remaining flicker noise is usually due to indirect mechanisms (like LO noise folding).
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 devices have standard flicker noise profiles; zero DC current topology will keep the corner frequency very low, matching the paper's claims.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench to measure the voltage Conversion Gain of the passive mixer. An RF signal at 5.001 GHz is mixed with a 5.000 GHz LO signal to produce a 1 MHz IF. A low-pass RC load filters out the high-frequency feedthrough, allowing the extraction of the IF amplitude.
step3_testbench.spice:
* CMOS Passive Mixer Testbench

.param W_xm2_n=5u L_xm2_n=0.5u
.param W_xm1_n=5u L_xm1_n=0.5u
.param W_xm1_p=5u L_xm1_p=0.5u
.param W_xm2_p=5u L_xm2_p=0.5u

* DUT
XM2_N IF_N LOCN N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2_n} w={W_xm2_n}
XM1_N IF_P LON N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1_n} w={W_xm1_n}
XM1_P IF_P N1 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1_p} w={W_xm1_p}
XM2_P IF_N N0 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2_p} w={W_xm2_p}

* Biasing and Signals
* RF and IF DC bias set to 0V to ensure Vgs > Vth when LO is high
V_IF_CM IF_CM 0 dc 0

* RF Source (5.001 GHz, 10mV peak)
VRF N2_ac 0 dc 0 sin(0 0.01 5.001G)
R_RF N2_ac N2 50

* LO Sources (5 GHz, 1.2V peak-to-peak, DC=0.75V)
VLO_P LO_P 0 dc 0.75 sin(0.75 0.6 5G 0 0 0)
VLO_N LO_N 0 dc 0.75 sin(0.75 0.6 5G 0 0 180)

* Connect LO to mixer gates (parallel transistors driven together for basic test)
R_LON LO_P LON 1
R_N1  LO_P N1  1
R_LOCN LO_N LOCN 1
R_N0   LO_N N0   1

* IF Load (Low pass filter to extract 1MHz IF, fc ~ 16MHz)
R_IFP IF_P IF_CM 10k
C_IFP IF_P IF_CM 1p
R_IFN IF_N IF_CM 10k
C_IFN IF_N IF_CM 1p

* Differential IF output for easy measurement
E_diff IF_DIFF 0 IF_P IF_N 1.0

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
  * Run transient for 2us (two periods of 1MHz IF)
  tran 10p 2u
  
  * Measure IF peak-to-peak (differential) in the steady-state region
  meas tran if_max max v(IF_DIFF) from=1u to=2u
  meas tran if_min min v(IF_DIFF) from=1u to=2u
  
  * Calculate Conversion Gain
  let if_pp = if_max - if_min
  let if_amp = if_pp / 2
  let rf_amp = 0.01
  let cg_linear = if_amp / rf_amp
  let cg_db = 20 * log10(cg_linear)
  
  print cg_db
  
  quit
.endc
.end
